supersedes.F6B00478EC422BCD: SUPERSEDED AND VOID. Its deduplication design was WRONG. It stated that setting transaction_id = lead_id on the Google Ads conversion would let a WhatConverts upload and the on-page tag deduplicate against each other. Google Ads does not deduplicate across different conversion actions, so that design would not have prevented the double count. Every other workstream in it remains valid and is carried forward here with corrected language.

CORRECTED_DEDUPLICATION_STATEMENT.retraction: An earlier statement in this engagement claimed a shared lead_id or transaction_id would deduplicate 'LP Submit Lead Forms' (6885463625) against 'WC Lead' (7643656486). THAT IS INCORRECT and is retracted.
CORRECTED_DEDUPLICATION_STATEMENT.what_lead_id_DOES_do: It prevents the SAME conversion action from recording the same event more than once. Within one action, a repeat fire carrying an already-seen order_id or transaction_id is discarded. That is genuinely valuable: it stops a confirmation re-render, a page reload or a back-navigation from inflating the count.
CORRECTED_DEDUPLICATION_STATEMENT.what_lead_id_DOES_NOT_do: It does NOT deduplicate two DIFFERENT conversion actions. Google Ads has no cross-action deduplication of any kind. Two actions each record independently regardless of any shared identifier.
CORRECTED_DEDUPLICATION_STATEMENT.why_merging_the_two_is_impossible_in_thi: Offline uploads require a conversion action of type UPLOAD_CLICKS or UPLOAD_CALLS. Verified from the Google Ads API: 6885463625 is WEBPAGE, 6885576934 is WEBSITE_CALL and 1068114183 is AD_CALL, so none of them can receive a WhatConverts upload. Only 7643656486 (UPLOAD_CLICKS) and 7643656075 (UPLOAD_CALLS) can. The tag signal and the upload signal therefore cannot be made to supplement one another.
CORRECTED_DEDUPLICATION_STATEMENT.enhanced_conversions_for_leads: enhanced_conversions_for_leads_enabled is TRUE and accepted_customer_data_terms is TRUE on this customer. That mechanism supplements an EXISTING web action with hashed first-party identifiers for better matching. It is not a route to merging a third-party upload action with a tag action.
CORRECTED_DEDUPLICATION_STATEMENT.the_only_reliable_control: Exactly ONE conversion action may be Primary AND included in the conversions metric per real-world lead event. That decision is made in Google Ads, in conversion Plan A or Plan B, NOT on the landing page.
CORRECTED_DEDUPLICATION_STATEMENT.so_what_is_this_package_for: Attribution capture, single-fire integrity within the form action, unique DOM ids, correct telephone markup and legal links. It makes the form signal trustworthy. It does not and cannot resolve the cross-action double count.

workstream_1_attribution_capture.problem: The Gravity Form posts only gform_source_page_number_1. No click identifier reaches the form, so a lead in the CRM cannot be tied to the click that produced it and no offline conversion can be uploaded against a gclid.
workstream_1_attribution_capture.capture_rule: On FIRST pageview of a session read each field from the URL query string. Persist to a first-party cookie AND sessionStorage. On later pageviews do NOT overwrite a non-empty stored value: first touch wins within the session, matching how Google attributes the click.

storage.fallback: sessionStorage key amb_attr where cookies are blocked

fields.name: lead_id
fields.source: BACKEND-generated opaque id returned on successful submission
fields.meaning: unique non-PII lead identifier and within-action dedup key

workstream_1_attribution_capture.lead_id_rule: Generate the lead identifier on the BACKEND when the submission is accepted, not in the browser. It must be opaque, unique, non-PII, and returned to the page so the confirmation can pass it to the dataLayer. A server-generated UUID v4 is fine. Backend generation prevents a client replay from minting a fresh id and slipping past the single-fire guard.
workstream_1_attribution_capture.preserve: gclid, gbraid, wbraid and all five UTMs must continue to be captured exactly as they are today. WhatConverts already captures them in its own cookies; this makes the Gravity Forms post carry them too.

workstream_2_single_fire_within_the_form.problem: Each page renders THREE Gravity Forms, all with DOM id gform_1. Duplicate ids are invalid HTML, break GTM triggers that select by id, and make it ambiguous which instance submitted.
workstream_2_single_fire_within_the_form.fix_a: Render exactly ONE functional Gravity Form per page. A second call to action must be an anchor to that form, never a second form instance.
workstream_2_single_fire_within_the_form.fix_b: Every rendered form and every field gets a unique DOM id. If more than one instance must render, suffix ids with the Gravity Forms instance number so no id repeats in the document.
workstream_2_single_fire_within_the_form.fix_c: Fire the conversion dataLayer event ONLY after a CONFIRMED SUCCESSFUL submission, that is after the backend has accepted the entry and returned a lead_id. Never on client-side validation success alone.
workstream_2_single_fire_within_the_form.fix_d: Guard the push with the returned lead_id so a confirmation re-render, reload or back-navigation cannot re-fire it: if (window.__ambFired === leadId) return; window.__ambFired = leadId;
workstream_2_single_fire_within_the_form.scope_of_benefit: This guarantees ONE fire of the FORM action per submission. It has no effect on any other conversion action.

workstream_3_datalayer_contract.gtm_trigger: Custom Event on amb_lead_submit with condition lead_id is not empty.
workstream_3_datalayer_contract.google_ads_tag: Bind to conversion action 6885463625. Set transaction_id = lead_id. ACCURATE SCOPE: this prevents 6885463625 from counting the same submission twice. It does NOT prevent 7643656486 WC Lead from also counting that submission. Only the Primary/Secondary decision in conversion Plan A or Plan B controls that.
workstream_3_datalayer_contract.ga4_tag: Send the same event to the existing G-9X9ZHNCRWF stream for diagnostics. GA4 actions are already Secondary and excluded from the conversions metric.
